items.synopsis: Major alarms for fabric link faults that result in reduced fabric capacity are introduced on PTX10004 and PTX10008 platforms
items.description: On Junos OS Evolved PTX10004 and PTX10008 platforms with LC1301 line cards and SF5 fabric, fabric link faults need to be reported as major alarms. Link faults can occur during system operation and result in reduced fabric capacity with partial impact. This enhancement introduces the new alarm "One or more PFE pairs operating with less than acceptable fabric capacity" to indicate reduced fabric capacity conditions.

items.category: Tracking interface specific issues for Aegon Line card
items.synopsis: Interfaces remain down on PTX10008/PTX10004 with LC1301 line cards when 2X100G speed is configured before QSFP optics insertion
items.description: On PTX10008 and PTX10004 platforms running Junos Evolved affected releases with LC1301 line cards, Ethernet interfaces remain down when the 2x100G interface speed is configured before Quad Small Formfactor Pluggable (QSFP) transceivers are inserted and the optical signal is up. This condition affects dataplane connectivity and can result in loss of traffic on the impacted interfaces.

items.synopsis: Junos EVO platform fails to recognize a SIB card after it experiences a power failure
items.description: On PTX10004, PTX10008 and PTX10016 platforms running Junos OS Evolved, when a Switch Interface Board (SIB) experiences a power failure and is later replaced with a healthy SIB, the device fails to recognize the installed SIB. The affected SIB slot remains in an Empty state, resulting in reduced switch fabric capacity, loss of fabric redundancy, and potential traffic impact under load.

items.synopsis: Link flapping occurs on stable subinterfaces when using QDD400GZR optics if any one subinterface in the channelized group is down
items.description: On all Junos OS Evolved platforms that support the QDD-400G-ZR coherent optical transceiver modules (400G-ZR and 400G OpenZR+), when an interface is equipped with any of these optics and configured in breakout mode, if anyone of the sub-interfaces in the group is administratively up and operationally down, the remaining stable sub-interfaces in the same group experience the link flaps at a regular interval.

items.synopsis: PICD process core observed on device
items.description: On all Junos OS Evolved platforms, due to software segmentation fault, optics firmware reports a max_lane_count greater than 8. This causes the picd process to core resulting in traffic loss. This is a rare issue.

items.synopsis: Ethernet-switching flood filter stops working when policer action is added
items.description: On BX-based Junos OS Evolved PTX platforms, when a flood filter with a policer is applied together with VLAN interface configuration in a single commit, the filter may not be properly installed, even though the commit is successful. As a result, the flood filter does not function as intended, leading to degraded traffic handling and performance issues.

items.synopsis: JDI-RCT:EVO: PTX10008-JNP10K-RE1-E128 - ERROR : evo-aftmand-bx core is seen and not able to backtrace the core during baseline validation
items.description: Filter rollback under high-scale conditions may trigger an unexpected evo-aftmand restart

items.synopsis: Physical interface creation failure was ignored resulting in system crash or traffic blackhole
items.description: On Junos OS Evolved PTX Series routers, during physical interface deactivate/activate operations, failure to recreate a physical Interface Device (IFD) resulted in an inconsistent interface state. This issue caused a system crash leading to service disruption or traffic blackhole.

items.synopsis: Traffic impact is observed due to rapid interface flapping on PTX12008 routers or devices equipped with JNP10K-LC1301 FPC or JNP10008-SF5 SIB modules
items.description: On Junos OS Evolved PTX12008 platform or devices equipped with JNP10K-LC1301 FPC (Flexible PIC Concentrator) or JNP10008-SF5 SIB (Switch Interface Board) cards, a rapid (sub-second) interface flap triggers a timing issue that causes the evo-cda-bx process to hog CPU resources. These periods of high CPU utilization affect other processes and protocols, ultimately impacting traffic on the device.

items.category: Junos Evolved Netstack Socket Intercept and NetIO libraries
items.synopsis: Locally originated TCP traffic egresses drained interface despite RIB/FIB pointing to right next-hop
items.description: On a Junos Evolved Routing Engine, TCP host traffic may use stale route state for egress.This fault may be seen for a TCP socket whose remote peer transitions from being reachable over an ECMP route to being reachable over a non-ECMP route.These conditions are necessary but not sufficient to produce the fault in which some TCP flows continue to use stale route state. The fault is not fully deterministic, as it is affected by the timing of events and by the results of ECMP load-balancing logic. The impact of the fault depends on the release. On releases from 24.4R2 and 25.2R1 onward, an established TCP flow may migrate from one ECMP link to another after a socket option is changed, but traffic will not be lost. If any route state changes (even for an unrelated route or interface), the next send or receive operation on a TCP socket will update the state for that flow to use the egress interface expected for the current route state. On older releases, the stale state may linger after the route state changes to no longer use ECMP, which can lead to packet drops and TCP retransmission.

items.synopsis: SNMP traps related to optics/optic's media lane alarms will not be raised
items.description: On Junos OS Evolved platforms, SNMP(Simple Network Management Protocol) management systems do not receive related to optics or transceiver lane and module alarm traps.

items.synopsis: ACX7020/ACX7024/ACX7024X/ ACX71xx/ACX73xx/ACX7509/Ufispace is not able to configure "no-temperature-monitoring" for ports higher than 23
items.description: ACX7020/ACX7024/ACX7024X/ ACX73xx/ACX7509/Ufispace is not able to configure "no-temperature-monitoring" for ports higher than 23

items.synopsis: Excessive xcvr config_mismatch DEBUG messages were generated in picd during periodic monitoring
items.description: On Junos EVO PTX Series platforms (PTX12008, PTX10001-36MR, and PTX10003-160C), when a transceiver (xcvr) configuration mismatch alarm was present, the picd periodic transceiver monitoring process generated repetitive DEBUG log messages. The issue was observed in environments containing transceivers reporting configuration mismatch alarms. During periodic monitoring, the same mismatch and alarm conditions were repeatedly logged, resulting in excessive growth of picd logs.

items.category: PTX10K Line Card specific interface PRs
items.synopsis: Incorrect module temperature readings trigger unintended optics shutdown
items.description: On MX platforms with MPC11, LC9600, LC4800 Linecards, MX304 and all Junos OS Evolved platforms, optics modules intermittently reports extremely high false temperature values in "show interfaces diagnostics optics" command. This can trigger false high-temperature alarms, leading to unnecessary optics shutdown.

items.synopsis: jnxOperatingState not reporting the correct value for FanTray after the FanTray Recovered from an error
items.description: Field Replaceable Unit (FRU) fault state was missing in the SNMP MIBs. This causes jnxOperatingState to return 1, which means 'unknown' instead of 2, which means 'running'

items.category: Software build tools (packaging, makefiles, et. al.)
items.synopsis: NETCONF: RPC get & get-configuration display invalid json format response for an OpenConfig when adds a routing-options configuration
items.description: After adding a "routing-options" configuration via OpenConfig operation, subsequent "get" and "get-configuration" may display an invalid JSON format.

items.category: Tracking interface specific issues for Aegon Line card
items.synopsis: Interfaces remain down on PTX10008/PTX10004 with LC1301 line cards when 2X100G speed is configured before QSFP optics insertion
items.description: On PTX10008 and PTX10004 platforms running Junos Evolved affected releases with LC1301 line cards, Ethernet interfaces remain down when the 2x100G interface speed is configured before Quad Small Formfactor Pluggable (QSFP) transceivers are inserted and the optical signal is up. This condition affects dataplane connectivity and can result in loss of traffic on the impacted interfaces.

items.synopsis: PTX10002-36QDD: evo-aftmand-bx "Out-of-order deletion of AftNode AftTunnelDecap" errors when changing route-distinguisher value on routing-instance
items.description: If you change an RD that you configured and committed previously, or change the routing instance type from virtual-router to vrf, make either of those changes during a maintenance window, as follows: Deactivate the routing instance. Change the RD. Activate the routing instance. If there is a filter installed with decap-action configured and the associated NH is part of the routing instance for which the route-distinguisher is changed without following the above steps, the filter could get into error state.

items.synopsis: jdhcpd.re.re0 cored at trace_file_close_internal (traceptr=0x7efc443b2bb0) at ../../src/junos_trace.c:188
items.description: When DHCP trace options are enabled, there is a possibility that jdhcpd could core. In general, traceoptions should be enabled only for debugging. They should be disabled once debuffing is done.

items.synopsis: The BUM traffic is looped back towards customer edge in EVPN-MPLS all-active multihoming environment due to missing ESI label encapsulation
items.description: On Junos OS Evolved ACX Series platforms configured in an EVPN-MPLS (Ethernet Virtual Private Network - Multiprotocol Label Switching) all-active multihoming environment using ESI-LAG (Ethernet Segment Identifier - Link Aggregation Group), when a BGP (Border Gateway Protocol) / BFD (Bidirectional Forwarding Detection) flap occurs between EVPN peers, BUM (Broadcast, Unknown-unicast, Multicast) traffic is sent back towards the same CE (Customer Edge) from which it was received due to missing ESI label encapsulation. As a result, BUM traffic is impacted and is not forwarded correctly.

items.synopsis: Multicast route programming fails on Junos OS Evolved ACX platforms with EVO_PFEMAND_ASIC_ PROGRAM_FAILED error
items.description: On Junos OS Evolved ACX platforms that configures IGMP (Internet Group Management Protocol) with IRB (Integrated Routing and Bridging) interfaces and IGMP snooping is enabled, during heavy IGMP join/leave churn, multicast route programming fails and the EVO_PFEMAND_ASIC_PROGRAM_FAILED error is observed. When this issue occurs, multicast hardware resource that is not correctly released, resulting in traffic disruption for all traffics associated with multicast routes.

items.synopsis: Multiple link flaps observed on all ACX7K platforms
items.description: On all ACX7K platforms, an internal ASIC interrupt was triggered in two different scenarios, in some cases the issue is seen without any change in the configuration and in some other cases the issue is seen when an egress sflow (sampled Flow) and egress mirror was enabled/attached to the same interface and committed. The triggered interrupt causes multiple interface flaps and temporary suspension of the ASIC programming resulting in transient disruption of forwarding operations and packet loss.

items.category: Issues related to evo operations - libevo infra, typeinfo ..
items.synopsis: Objmon Memory Leak from Unreleased IndexReleaseConfirm Objects leads to distributord Out of memory and Router Reboot
items.description: On all Junos Evolved PTX platforms, long-term use of PFEtoken features triggers an objmon memory leak, where net:: juniper:: evlruntime:: indexrelease:: IndexReleaseConfirm objects are not properly released, causing distributord to be OOM (Out of Memory) and killed due to memory exhaustion.

items.synopsis: In an EVPN Flex Algorithm environment, if multiple routing instances share the same color and the same VLAN, traffic may not be handled correctly
items.description: In an EVPN Flex algorithm environment, if multiple routing instances share the same color and VLAN, there is a possibility that traffic may not be processed correctly. Under such circumstances, the bridged domains within the routing instances may end up sharing the same VSI, which can result in traffic being directed to unintended routing instances.

items.category: Issues related to NTP issues on evo
items.synopsis: Nagios server not able to connect to ACX7024X
items.description: On EVO ACX platforms with VRF/loopback/vrrp when ntpd replies to client requests the NTP server responses uses incorrect source addresses instead of the destination address of the received packet, causing NTP client queries to fail or receive responses from unexpected source addresses.

items.synopsis: PAA installation failure on reboot due to "Not found default vrf" error
items.description: When a device is rebooted with PAA installed in 25.2R1 , PAA installation on reboot may fail due to "Not found default vrf" error. This can be resolved by deactivating and activating or freshly installing the PAA configuration

items.synopsis: SNMP traps related to optics/optic's media lane alarms will not be raised
items.description: On Junos OS Evolved platforms, SNMP(Simple Network Management Protocol) management systems do not receive related to optics or transceiver lane and module alarm traps.

items.synopsis: Intermittent "broadsync_lock_failure" alarms are seen on Junos OS Evolved ACX platforms
items.description: On Junos OS Evolved ACX platforms, "broadsync_lock_failure" alarms are seen intermittently without any external trigger. These alarms are seen as a result of internal firmware misconfiguration and affects PTP (Precision Time Protocol) functionality. The alarms are cleared after few seconds (~10 secs) once the broadsync lock is restored.

items.synopsis: PTP delay message sent from different LAG after RE switchover
items.description: On Junos OS Evolved ACX7332 and ACX7348 platforms, after Routing Engines( RE) switchover the Precision Time Protocol (PTP) delay message is sent from different REs when Link Aggregation Group (LAG) members are configured on different Flexible PIC Concentrators (FPCs) leading to PTP timing discrepancy.

items.category: Category for JET(JUNOS Extension Toolkit) related issues
items.synopsis: Removal of the suffix when the hostname is used as the target ID in the gRPC-tunnel configuration
items.description: On all Junos Evolved platforms, when hostname is used as the target ID in the gRPC-tunnel configuration, it includes the routing engine information as a suffix ("-re0" or "-re1"), the suffix part is now removed. is now removed. This issue has no impact on traffic.

items.category: Category for JET(JUNOS Extension Toolkit) related issues
items.synopsis: System connections are not established while Subscribing for OC path using ssl local-certificates after upgrading to 24.4R2-S3-EVO
items.description: System connections are not established while Subscribing for OC path using ssl local-certificates after upgrading to 24.4R2-S3-EVO. This issue is only applicable on 24.4R2-S3-EVO and 24.4R2-S4-EVO

items.synopsis: MPLS auto-policing fails to drop excess IPv6 traffic on P2MP RSVP-TE LSPs
items.description: On Junos and Junos EVO platforms the MPLS auto-policing function fails to drop excess IPv6 traffic on Resource Reservation Protocol P2MP LSP (Label Switched Paths). Although the policer is correctly applied for IPv4 P2MP (Point to Multipoint) LSP the IPv6 equivalent fails because the flood-nexthop (floodNH) does not contain the auto-policer information. This issue leads to oversubscription and unpredictable QoS behavior.

items.category: Transport daemon for Packet Optical applications
items.synopsis: Optical performance monitoring becomes unavailable on PTX platforms with high scale of coherent-ZR interfaces
items.description: On Junos Evolved PTX platforms, systems with approximately 240 or more interfaces configured on ports using coherent-ZR optics (such as 100ZR and 400ZR transceivers) experience a loss of optical performance monitoring functionality. As a result, optical performance monitoring data, alarms, and statistics are no longer available through management interfaces.

items.synopsis: The rdp process crash after executing "clear ospf database" when OSPF Remote Loop-Free Alternate RLFA is configured
items.description: The software issue occurs during Open Shortest Path First (OSPF) Remote Loop-Free Alternate (RLFA) route calculation. One way to trigger the issue is by executing the "clear ospf database" CLI command.

items.synopsis: The rpd process crashes when processing multipath routes with mixed indirect and composite next-hops under rib-sharding
items.description: On all Junos and Junos OS Evolved platforms, when rib-sharding is enabled and RT (Route Target) multipath routes containing both indirect and composite next-hop types are processed, the rpd (Routing Protocol Daemon) process will crash due to incorrect handling during the next-hop copy operation from RIB (Routing Information Base) shards to the main RIB thread. An rpd crash results in all routing protocols going down and causes a brief traffic disruption until the rpd process restarts.

items.synopsis: RSVP detour LSP does not follow configured FRR admin-group exclusion constraints
items.description: On Junos OS and Junos OS Evolved platforms, when MPLS (Multiprotocol Label Switching), RSVP (Resource Reservation Protocol), dynamic tunnels, and an LSP (Label-Switched Path) template with FRR (Fast Reroute) admin-group exclusion constraints are configured, the detour LSP does not follow the configured exclusions after the primary LSP becomes unavailable. The detour LSP uses an unintended path, while traffic and services remain unaffected.

items.synopsis: EVO: RPC "get-power-usage-information" for cli "show chassis power" shows error wtih ODL response
items.description: RPC "get-power-usage-information" for cli "show chassis power" shows error wtih ODL response

items.synopsis: Incorrect allocated power values are returned via telemetry
items.description: Due to missing capdb change, telemetry incorrectly reports the allocated power values for RCB and fan tray.

items.category: Configuration mgmt, ffp, load-action, commit processing
items.synopsis: Netconf RPC commit fails due to commit warning received for unprotect operation, CLI commit completes with warning
items.description: In Netconf private edit configuration session, commit RPC fails when unprotect operation is performed.

items.category: PRs related to PICd and associated lib WAN side PI code.
items.synopsis: PICD fails to reuse or clean SNMP trap objects, causing memory leak
items.description: On all Junos OS Evolved platforms, PICD repeatedly created new SNMP trap objects without removing old ones, causing distributord memory leaks over time. This is tracked under TSB107540
